Everything checks out — this task is already complete on `origin/main`. Let me summarize what I found rather than duplicate the work.

**V-654 is already done and pushed to `origin/main`** as commit `2f78aac0` ("restore quota history lines and time labels"), by another worker session — this worktree (`v656/quota-s5`) was still sitting one commit behind (at V-652's `8aa733f5`).

I verified it independently rather than trusting the report blindly:

1. **Root cause matches what I found by reproducing the bug myself.** I loaded the real live JSON (`data/v654/quota-map-live.json`) into a Playwright harness with the pre-fix JS: the threshold-cycle builder was treating every snapshot's `resets_at` (which drifts slightly between samples) as a distinct window boundary, generating hundreds of overlapping policy zigzags that visually buried the thin actual-usage lines underneath — matching your screenshot exactly (smooth curves only, no staircase history, missing Claude point).

2. **The fix is correct.** It reverted the cycle-builder to use only the canonical `window.resets_at`/`window_minutes`, and draws the real `timeline.points` history as a separate polyline. I reran the same live JSON through the fixed JS — history lines (169/171 points) and all current-value points now render.

3. **X-axis labels match your spec**: ticks every 2h (84 ticks across the ±3.5-day range), text every 4h to avoid crowding, and 00:00/08:00 boundaries always get a two-line weekday+time label. Their test asserts zero bounding-box overlap between any two labels.

4. **Tests**: I ran the full suite in an isolated worktree at that commit — the new test `test_live_quota_map_history_and_two_hour_labels` passes. 12 other tests fail, but I confirmed by running the same suite at the pre-V-654 parent commit that those exact 12 failures pre-exist (a Russian-literal/English-render mismatch unrelated to this change) — not a regression.

5. Screenshot, CHANGELOG entry, and `.orchestra/tasks/V-654/report.md` are all present and accurate in that commit; the old chart below is untouched.

Since your git rule is "existing work by others is preserved, no auto-merge," I didn't touch this worktree's branch state. Nothing left to implement here — this worktree can be closed as redundant. Want me to do anything else with it (e.g., sync it to main, or leave it as-is for cleanup)?
